source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's POR03 campus in Hillsboro occupies 182,000 square feet of technical space, but without a published power figure, its capacity for AI workloads cannot be determined.

The absence of a megawatt rating prevents any assessment of how many AI racks this facility could support. Technical space alone does not correlate to compute density. A 182,000-square-foot floor could house anywhere from dozens to hundreds of high-density AI clusters depending on power allocation and cooling architecture, both unpublished. Without critical IT load data, POR03 cannot be ranked among Oregon's six facilities that do disclose capacity, which together account for 182 MW.

This data gap is common across Oregon's 133 mapped facilities. Many operators publish no specifications at all. POR03 lists no certifications, so its redundancy tier and compliance posture are unknown. Interconnection details, pricing, and tenant information are also withheld from public view.

For an AI infrastructure analyst, the square footage is only a starting point. The binding constraint on AI scaling is compute, which flows from buildings with sufficient power and cooling. A facility's power rating, not its floor area, determines its relevance to AI deployment. Until Stack Infrastructure publishes a power figure for POR03, the campus remains opaque to capacity planning.
